items.stem: A technician asks a patient for their current medicines, allergy history, and date of birth. An interaction alert then appears. Which actions are within the described roles? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Record the patient's factual answers in the profile for pharmacist review.
choices.why: Correct. Staff may assist with factual intake and profile information; the pharmacist retains professional responsibility.

choices.text: Resolve the interaction alert by deciding the drug combination is clinically safe.
choices.why: Incorrect. A technician may not perform DUR or resolve a clinical conflict.

choices.text: Refer the alert and any inconsistent allergy information to the pharmacist before dispensing.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacist must make the prospective DUR and take appropriate measures for identified problems.

choices.text: Give the patient the final therapeutic counseling based on the technician's own interpretation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pharmacy technicians may not provide patient counseling.

items.novelty_rationale: Asks for two affirmative workflow actions rather than repeating a roster of prohibited duties.

items.stem: At a community pharmacy staffed by one pharmacist, the pharmacist has started a 20-minute meal break in a back room but remains inside the pharmacy premises, as permitted by the pharmacy's written policy. Before the break, the pharmacist personally completed the final check and prospective DUR on a patient's NEW prescription. The patient arrives now to collect it; the technical staff have not started a new clinical review. What additional pickup workflow does 247 CMR 9.19 require?

choices.text: A second pharmacist must come on duty before the prepared prescription can be collected.
choices.why: Incorrect. The break provision permits a specifically conditioned handoff without another pharmacist for a solo pharmacy.

choices.text: Log the pickup and phone number, then arrange pharmacist follow-up.
choices.why: Correct. A checked new prescription may be collected with a transaction log including phone number and timely pharmacist follow-up.

choices.text: The technician may complete any unfinished clinical DUR and release the drug.
choices.why: Incorrect. The clinical DUR must already have been completed by the pharmacist before pickup.

choices.text: The pharmacist may leave the building if the prescription was checked before the break.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacist must remain on the pharmacy premises throughout this exception.

items.novelty_rationale: Tests the log and post-break counseling for a previously validated new prescription, not simply the break duration.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has three years of licensed experience, completed an accredited clinical residency, and wants to enter a CDTM agreement. The pharmacist has no pre-July 2017 PharmD agreement. Who must determine whether the residency substitutes for five years of experience?

choices.text: The Board, under its education-or-residency equivalency pathway.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation expressly assigns determination of equivalence to the Board.

choices.text: The collaborating physician, through a signed statement in the agreement.
choices.why: Incorrect. Physician agreement cannot replace the Board's equivalency decision.

choices.text: The residency director, by certifying two years of additional experience.
choices.why: Incorrect. Training verification alone is not the specified Board determination.

choices.text: The pharmacist, after documenting a personal equivalency assessment.
choices.why: Incorrect. Self-assessment does not satisfy an equivalency that the Board must determine.

items.novelty_rationale: Distinguishes who authorizes residency equivalence, rather than testing only the five-year threshold.

items.stem: An Idaho-licensed pharmacist receives NABP approval for transfer, passes the Massachusetts MPJE, and receives an employment offer. The Massachusetts Board has not yet issued a pharmacist license. When may this person practice as a Massachusetts pharmacist?

choices.text: Immediately after NABP approval, since NABP performs the initial transfer evaluation.
choices.why: Incorrect. NABP evaluates applications but the Board makes the licensure decision.

choices.text: Immediately upon passing the MPJE, provided the employer retains the score report.
choices.why: Incorrect. Passing an exam is not itself an active pharmacist license.

choices.text: When the Massachusetts Board grants an active pharmacist license.
choices.why: Correct. Board-issued Massachusetts licensure is required to practice in the state.

choices.text: On the date the employer sends the signed offer to the Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. An employment offer cannot create pharmacist licensure.

items.novelty_rationale: Focuses on the licensing event, not the application/eligibility calculations used elsewhere.

items.stem: A pharmacist reports taking a lawfully prescribed sedative, but on this shift is visibly confused and repeatedly selects the wrong product. Which action best addresses the immediate pharmacy-law concern?

choices.text: Take no action until a patient is injured, since the medication was prescribed.
choices.why: Incorrect. Actual unsafe performance warrants action without waiting for harm.

choices.text: Treat any use of a prescribed sedative as automatic permanent loss of the pharmacist's license.
choices.why: Incorrect. The relevant issue is safe practice, not automatic loss of licensure from lawful medication use.

choices.text: Continue filling as long as a technician catches each wrong selection before release.
choices.why: Incorrect. Delegation does not remove the pharmacist's safe-practice and final-validation responsibilities.

choices.text: Stop unsafe dispensing and arrange appropriate coverage while the impairment is evaluated.
choices.why: Correct. A pharmacist must practice safely; observed incapacity creates a direct patient-safety concern.

items.novelty_rationale: Tests observed unsafe performance versus mere lawful medication use; makes no unsupported automatic reporting claim.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy-technician applicant truthfully discloses an old misdemeanor unrelated to drugs, with no drug-related felony conviction or admission to sufficient facts. Which conclusion follows from 247 CMR 8.02?

choices.text: The misdemeanor is sufficient to trigger the drug-felony bar based on its mere existence.
choices.why: Incorrect. The stated disqualifying category specifically concerns drug-related felonies or qualifying admissions.

choices.text: The applicant should omit the event because the application is submitted to a professional Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. Truthful disclosure and good-character review remain relevant to licensure.

choices.text: The drug-felony bar is not shown; other licensing requirements still apply.
choices.why: Correct. The listed conviction/admission restriction is narrower than all criminal history, while other criteria still apply.

choices.text: The Board must license the applicant immediately because the misdemeanor is not drug-related.
choices.why: Incorrect. Other eligibility and good-moral-character requirements still apply; licensure is not automatic.

items.novelty_rationale: Distinguishes a narrow statutory disqualification from the rest of the applicant's required evaluation.

qa_note: Novelty and all A-D explanations need final law source-by-source approval; no public Form C exam release.
authoring_edit: B4 second-pass style repair: shorter correct alternatives, diversified stem lengths, repaired extreme-word hints; no change to answer keys.
